provenance.instrument: Township of Brighton Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 195 Zoning, Ord. No. 96 of 10-14-1996, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BR1789, Township of Brighton, Beaver County (195-10 'Governing body': 'The Board of Township Supervisors, of the Township of Brighton, Beaver County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles V to XII. The attachments are a sign illustration and buffer yard exhibits only. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 100. New Laws: Ord. No. 252 of 2026-08-10 (Fire Prevention Code), not on zoning
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 01-12-2026.' New Laws: one, Ord. No. 252 of 2026-08-10 (Fire Prevention Code)
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, household employee, conversion apartment, residential conversion, temporary dwelling, apartment addition, habitation, living quarters, caretaker, mobile home) find only the definitions of a conversion apartment unit and a residential conversion unit (195-10) and the mobile home rules (195-134)

R-1, R-2, UD and SC-1 each permit 'One single-family detached dwelling per lot' (195-16A(1), 195-24A(4), 195-32A(1), 195-80A(2)). No district lists a second unit on a house lot. A second unit is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (195-157). No bar on a use variance was found

Where a use is neither permitted nor prohibited in a district, the Zoning Officer decides its status, with an appeal to the Zoning Hearing Board (195-4A). A use not listed in any district is referred to the Zoning Hearing Board and 'shall be reviewed as a request for a special exception in the C-2 Mixed Use District' (195-4B). C-2 permits no single-family dwelling, so this does not open a path on a house lot. Only uses listed as special exceptions in a district may be considered there (195-157.1A(1)). A conversion apartment unit is listed (R-1), so a unit made inside a house is not an unlisted use

Conversion apartment unit: a conditional use in R-1 only, before the Board of Supervisors after a hearing and Planning Commission review (195-17A, 195-163, 195-164). It is 'The remodeling of a single-family dwelling unit into two or more separate living units each having a minimum of 500 square feet of habitable area, exclusive of basement and/or cellar dwellings; one bathroom and three habitable rooms; separate and private water, sanitary, cooking and dining facilities; and a minimum of two off-street parking spaces per living unit' (195-10). A conversion must stay inside the existing structural shell. Extending the sides or height is not a conversion and must meet the district's provisions for that use (195-10 'Dwelling type' A)

In R-1 the yards for a conditional use are larger than for a permitted use: front 50 ft from a collector or arterial and 40 ft from a local street, and 30 ft on each side (195-20B, D). Rear 40 ft for both. The yard rules 'shall apply to all permitted and conditional uses' in R-1 (195-20), so a house converted under 195-17A reads as needing the conditional use yards, or a variance

Duplex: R-1 permits a duplex, 'either side by side or over and under', by right with public sewer and public water, on 8,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, 125 ft wide, coverage 35% (195-16A(2), 195-19B). UD permits a single-family semidetached dwelling (duplex) by right with public sewer and water, on 7,500 sq ft per duplex unit and 100 ft of width for each unit, coverage 35% (195-32A(2), 195-35B). A duplex is two units side by side with a party wall, or one over the other with two side yards (195-10 'Dwelling type' C)

Accessory uses may not occupy more than 15% of the lot, and 'in no event shall the square feet of an accessory use structure exceed the total square feet of the principal use structure' (195-10 'Accessory use'). Required yards stay open 'except for accessory buildings in the rear yard and fences' (195-120A). Accessory side and rear yards: R-1 and UD 5 ft for a structure of 720 sq ft or less and 10 ft above that, R-2 and SC-1 10 ft (195-20F, 195-36A(4), 195-28F, 195-83). SC-1 accessory height 20 ft (195-85B)
Parking: 'Residential units: 2 off-street parking spaces per dwelling unit' (195-105B, 195-22, 195-30, 195-86). No rule for a fraction of a space was found

SC-1 opens with 'A lot or parcel may be used and a building or structure may be erected and used for any of the following purposes, subject to the granting of a use by the Township of Brighton Board of Supervisors' (195-80), and all building permits there are reviewed by the Township (195-81A)

Nonconforming lot: a single-family detached dwelling and customary accessory structures may be built on a single nonconforming lot in separate ownership. Yard relief needs a variance (195-140A, 195-125). Abutting nonconforming lots in one ownership must be combined (195-140B)

Mobile or modular homes 'shall be temporarily parked and stored or permanently parked and stored in mobile or modular home parks only' (195-124A), while R-2 permits mobile homes on individual lots under 195-134 as the one dwelling on the lot (195-24A(5))

Floodplain (Chapter 100): a permit is needed for any construction or development in the township (100-8). In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office', and no development may raise the base flood elevation at any point (100-18A(2)(b), 100-31E). New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (100-23A). Fill is prohibited with no variance (100-24A). An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may be at most 200 sq ft (100-23E). The Zoning Hearing Board hears floodplain appeals (100-16, 195-155F)

Front yards depend on the road: 30 ft from a local street, the figure stored for each district. On a collector or arterial road the front yard is 40 ft in R-1, UD and SC-1 and 50 ft in R-2 (195-20A, 195-28A, 195-36A(1), 195-83A(1)). Where at least 40% of the block frontage has deeper front yards, new buildings may not be closer to the street than that established front yard (195-120C)

A nonconforming residential structure may be enlarged if the addition comes no closer to the lot line and the existing yards are at least 80% of the district's front yard, 70% of its rear yard and 60% of its side yard (195-143A(1)). It may be altered within the confines of the existing buildings (195-143A(2))

Boardinghouse: up to two persons lodged for hire in sleeping rooms with a resident owner. A conditional use in R-1 and R-2 and by right in UD (195-10, 195-17H, 195-25R, 195-32A(15)). It is lodging, not a dwelling unit

HC-1 permits hospitals, nursing homes and other health care uses, residential units owned and operated by government agencies, a continuing care retirement community and farms, with senior housing as a conditional use. It permits no single-family house (195-72, 195-74I). R-1 planned residential developments allow houses, duplexes and townhouses, and no accessory unit (195-46)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Brighton Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: Articles I to III, Articles V to XIII, XVI, XVIII and XX, Article XV from 195-118 to 195-135B(12) and 195-137.17, Chapter 100 Articles I to VIII, the New Laws page, the table of contents and code searches. Not read: Article XIV (signs), Article XV from 195-135B(13) to 195-137.20 except 195-137.17 (home occupations, boardinghouse standards and other specific uses), Articles XVII, XIX and XXI to XXIII, and Chapter 180. Open points: whether the R-1 conditional use yards bind a house converted inside its shell (195-20 reads yes), and the UD duplex width of 100 ft 'for each duplex unit' (100 ft or 200 ft for the pair).

status.note: No district lists a second unit on a house lot. R-1, R-2, UD and SC-1 permit one single-family detached dwelling per lot. In R-1 a house may be converted into two or more units by conditional use (195-17A)

path.note: A second unit on a house lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). The review of a use not listed anywhere as a special exception reaches only the C-2 District (195-4B). In R-1 a house may instead be converted by conditional use, and a duplex may be built where the district permits one (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 195-157E(1) to (5). No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion apartment unit (R-1)
value.conditions: The remodeling of a single-family dwelling into two or more separate living units, each with at least 500 sq ft of habitable area not counting a basement or cellar, one bathroom and three habitable rooms, separate and private water, sanitary, cooking and dining facilities, and at least two off-street parking spaces per unit. The work must stay inside the existing structural shell. The Board of Supervisors decides after a public hearing and Planning Commission review, and may attach conditions. The R-1 yards for a conditional use apply: front 40 ft from a local street (50 ft from a collector or arterial), 30 ft on each side and 40 ft in the rear. A house that does not meet them needs a variance. The code gives no lot area for a conversion apartment unit

requires.condition: An existing single-family dwelling to remodel

value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it. The R-1 yard rules 'shall apply to all permitted and conditional uses', so the conditional use yards read as binding a converted house. Altering a nonconforming structure inside its walls (195-143A(2)) does not lift them for the new use. Ask the zoning officer

value.name: Duplex (R-1)
value.conditions: A duplex, 'either side by side or over and under', with public sanitary sewerage and public water service. Lot 8,000 sq ft per dwelling unit (16,000 sq ft for two), 125 ft wide at the building line, coverage with accessory structures at most 35%. Front 30 ft from a local street (40 ft from a collector or arterial), 10 ft on each side, rear 40 ft. Two parking spaces per unit. An addition that extends the sides or height of a house to make a second unit is not a conversion and must meet the district's provisions for that use. A house that does not meet the district yards may still be enlarged if the addition comes no closer to the lot line and its yards are at least 80% of the front, 70% of the rear and 60% of the side yard figures (195-143A(1))

requires.condition: A lot at least 125 ft wide at the building line

value.note: A two-unit building. Read for a house enlarged into a duplex, since 195-10 sends an extension of an existing structure to the district's provisions for the use it becomes

value.name: Single-family semidetached dwelling, duplex (UD)
value.conditions: A single-family semidetached dwelling (duplex) with public sanitary sewage and public water. Lot 7,500 sq ft per duplex unit (15,000 sq ft for two), 100 ft wide at the building line for each duplex unit, coverage with accessory structures at most 35%. Front 30 ft from a local street (40 ft from a collector or arterial), 10 ft on each side, rear 40 ft. A duplex is two units side by side with a party wall, or one over the other with two side yards

requires.condition: A lot at least 100 ft wide at the building line. The code asks 100 ft 'for each duplex unit', which may mean 200 ft for the pair

value.note: A two-unit building. UD lists no conversion apartment unit, so whether a house divided inside its shell counts as a duplex there is not settled. The 100 ft of width 'for each duplex unit' may mean 200 ft for the pair

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path was found in the parts read

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. HC-1, C-1 and C-2 permit no single-family dwelling. HC-1 permits residential units owned and operated by government agencies, a continuing care retirement community and farms, with senior housing by conditional use. C-1 and C-2 allow homes only above the first floor of a mixed-use building, and C-2 residential uses only within a mixed-use development

value.condition: R-1, R-2, UD and SC-1 permit 'One single-family detached dwelling per lot'. A second house on the lot is not a permitted use.

An accessory structure in an identified floodplain area 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation but shall be limited to the parking of vehicles or to the storage of tools, material, and equipment', with at most 200 sq ft of floor area and no sanitary facilities.

In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office'.

In a floodway no encroachment, new construction or substantial improvement unless an analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction without a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway no development may raise the base flood elevation at any point. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. Fill is prohibited, with no variance. Work costing 50% or more of the building's market value is a substantial improvement.

The district front yard is 30 ft from a local street. On a collector or arterial road it is 40 ft in R-1, UD and SC-1 and 50 ft in R-2. Where at least 40% of the block frontage has deeper front yards, a new building may not be closer to the street than that front yard.
